links.outcome: Model agreement on static benchmark versus temporally later post-cutoff cohort
links.effect: Fine-tuning improved agreement with reference labels on the static benchmark, but larger general-purpose models performed better on the heterogeneous post-cutoff cohort.
links.quote: Fine-tuning improved agreement with CIViC-Fact reference labels on the static benchmark, but larger general-purpose models performed better on a heterogeneous post-cutoff cohort.

unlisted_practices: Using full-text rather than abstract-only evidence for biomedical claim verification (fewer than 30% of entries fully validated from abstract alone)
Automated evidence retrieval for newly submitted knowledgebase entries (93% success)
Lightweight updating of verification systems via small high-quality few-shot exemplar sets

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates CIViC-Fact, a benchmark dataset and evaluation framework for AI-assisted verification of cancer variant claims from full-text literature.
